items.title: Europe pays the price in a summer where heat went off the charts
items.description: Western Europe is on fire, and authorities are already calling it the worst fire season in modern history. But there are no surprises.

items.title: The US may have reached 'turning point' in school shooting punishments
items.description: For the third time in US history, a parent has been held criminally responsible for the murderous actions of their child. Legal experts have suggested it marks a turning point for American prosecutors.

items.title: UTI led to Sydney woman's death three days after giving birth
items.description: Gia Lam gave birth to her son and was dead three days later. A coronial inquest found her death was preventable. Her family are now breaking their silence.

items.title: 'What's happened to me?': Bearing witness as my nan faced dementia
items.description: The woman who once chased down a donkey to save her granddaughter would one day need saving herself — and teach me a lesson about love.

items.title: 'People are really suffering': Ukraine's drones bring war home to Russia
items.description: For years, people in Russia's largest and most affluent cities were shielded from the impacts of their country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, but not anymore.

items.title: 'Pattern of missteps': Football bodies launch stunning Infantino rebuke
items.description: Two of football's major bodies launch stinging rebukes of FIFA president Gianni Infantino after his failed privatisation ploy.

items.title: One final clean sweep proves Aussie track stars are the real deal
items.description: Abbey Caldwell, Jess Hull and Claudia Hollingsworth's podium sweep of the women's mile to close the Glasgow athletics program marked a coming of age for the once and future stars of Australian athletics.

items.title: Quick hits: Sprinter's surprise, a bored prince and a stunning upset
items.description: Prince George looks utterly disinterested, Jamaican netballers celebrate and Australian sprinter's surprise visit. Here are the quick hits from day nine of the Commonwealth Games.

items.title: Trump's new respect for Zelenskyy highlights Netanyahu's problem
items.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy must have felt a little triggered when he walked into the Oval Office this week. But Trump's public anger is now often directed at another at-war ally.

items.title: To prove how easy it is to buy unregulated peptides the ABC organised a deal
items.description: The injectable drugs have not been approved for use in Australia but are advertised widely on social media.

items.title: Trump and Iran exchange threats on further strikes
items.description: Iran says any aggression by the US and Israel will be met with a proportionate response.

items.title: Spain slams 'selfish' EU, sets up floating barriers
items.description: European Union states are demanding stricter international border controls and have called an emergency meeting as Spain reassures safety of Schengen Area.

items.title: Voters are starting to ask a new question about politics, money
items.description: Debate about money in politics has traditionally revolved around whether politicians have broken the rules. But voters are increasingly asking what good judgement looks like.

items.title: 'A tsunami of need': Inside the fight over NDIS appeal rights
items.description: Appealing NDIS decisions is already difficult, but advocates fear it is about to become even harder for "incredibly vulnerable" people.

items.title: The secret formula that makes Eastern Rosellas the perfect earworm
items.description: Eastern Rosellas by seven-year-old Miles and his dad Joel Phillips is the perfect song you can't get out of your head. Experts in stage and academia say the ingredients are all there.

items.title: 'Wannabe' a music quiz legend? Right this way...
items.description: Hey ya! It's your time to shine with the Spicks and Specks quiz.

items.title: A rich, decadent chocolate cake with a surprising ingredient
items.description: This moist, dark cake has an almost earthy richness and is perfect for those who don't love their desserts super sweet.

items.title: Prices to jump at the bowser as fuel excise cut ends tonight
items.description: The price of unleaded and diesel will climb in the next week as the government's fuel excise cut officially ends. But experts say prices won't go as high as they did due to increased supply.

items.title: 'We're blowing this thing into the harbour': 50 years since woodchip bombing
items.description: A stolen car full of explosives, a hostage held at gunpoint, and a plan gone awry. Inside the anti-woodchip bombing at WA's Bunbury port in 1976.

items.title: Fifth-generation farm at a standstill due to contamination
items.description: The future of Kate Tucker’s family farm looks as murky as its waterways, which face a raft of contamination issues, but poor environmental regulation has left her with few options.

items.title: How people are looking outside the box to combat crippling housing crisis
items.description: From Tasmania to Broken Hill and the Northern Rivers of NSW, people are finding ways to beat the housing crisis.

items.title: Victoria's tobacco kingpin is in jail, but violence still grips the state
items.description: Kazem Hamad, once dubbed one of the most dangerous wanted men in the world, is now behind bars. But the violence on Victorian streets has continued unabated.

items.title: Home owners worry about proposed 40m telco tower going up next door
items.description: West Australian residents living beside a bush block where a 40-metre telecommunications tower could be built say they have been ignored in the planning process.

items.title: Radical idea to stop dust storms in this outback city has been a success for 50 years
items.description: Dust storms would blanket the sky and send people running indoors in this outback mining city. Fifty years ago, one man arrived in town with a radical idea that changed Kalgoorlie-Boulder.

items.title: Alex Antic’s long quest for Liberal Party influence reaches crunch time
items.description: After years building a power base within the SA division, the right-wing senator is the frontrunner to become the Liberal Party’s state president. It could have wide-ranging implications for Angus Taylor and Ashton Hurn.
